newsitem.title: USA: Ford's Trotman says no successor picked yet.
newsitem.headline: Ford's Trotman says no successor picked yet.

text.p: Ford Motor Co issued a statement Monday in which Chairman Alex Trotman said no decisions have been made about who will succeed him as chairman, and no candidates have been ruled out.
Ford said Trotman's comments were made in response to published reports about whether a Ford family member will succeed Trotman as the company's next chairman.

The Wall Street Journal, citing people close to the succession issue, reported Monday the board is considering naming either William "Bill" Clay Ford Jr. or Edward Hagenlocker, president of Ford's worldwide automotive operations, as its next chairman.

Bill Ford, 39 years old, is a great grandson of founder Henry Ford, and a member of the Ford Motor Co board. If Bill Ford is named chairman, then Hagenlocker would report to him as chief executive officer, according to the report.
The story also said Trotman, who is president and chief executive in addition to chairman, had not been asked to stay past his 65th birthday in 1998.
However, Fortune magazine issued a press release Friday, September 20, saying a story in its upcoming October 14 edition will report that Trotman has been asked to stay past his 65th birthday.

Fortune also said it will report that Bill Ford is a candidate to be the next chairman, and that Hagenlocker will be replaced in his current job by Jacques Nasser, who now heads product development operations.

In his statement Monday, Trotman said, "Right now it is too early for the board to decide on my successor. It is also done privately -- an old expression applies here -- 'those who know don't say, those who say don't know.'"
Trotman noted that some of his predecessors as chief executive have retired on, before and after their 65th birthdays. He said there are several candidates the board expects to consider as chairman.
"It's important that all the candidates get the right experience until the selection is made -- which will be much closer to my retirement," Trotman said.
A Ford spokesman on Friday denied the company had decided to bypass Hagenlocker as its next chairman and chief executive, and denied that he would be replaced in his current job by Nasser.
